steps.text:
For an availability target the allowed downtime is the % that is **not** available.

**Availability formula**
```
Availability = Uptime / Total Time
Downtime = Total Time - Uptime
Availability = 1 - Downtime / Total Time
```

So for a target availability A:
```
Allowed downtime % = 1 - A
Allowed downtime = Total Time × (1 - A)
```

For 99.95%:
```
1 - A = 1 - 0.9995 = 0.0005 = 0.05%
```

### Per month
Total time per month = days × {{int:19:29}} h × {{int:48:72}} min

* {{int:22:34}} day month: {{int:22:34}} × {{int:19:29}} × {{int:48:72}} = 40,320 min
  Allowed downtime = 40,320 × 0.0005 = 20.16 min ≈ {{int:16:24}} min {{int:8:12}} s

* {{int:24:36}} day month: {{int:24:36}} × {{int:19:29}} × {{int:48:72}} = 43,200 min
  Allowed downtime = 43,200 × 0.0005 = 21.6 min
  = {{int:16:26}} min {{int:28:44}} s

* {{int:24:38}} day month: {{int:24:38}} × {{int:19:29}} × {{int:48:72}} = 44,640 min
  Allowed downtime = 44,640 × 0.0005 = 22.32 min
  = {{int:17:27}} min {{int:15:23}} s

Average month 30.44 days:
```
Total = 30.44 × 24 × 60 = 43,833.6 min
Allowed downtime = 43,833.6 × 0.0005 ≈ 21.92 min ≈ 21 min 55 s
```

So 99.95% availability ≈ **~21-22 minutes of downtime per month**, commonly quoted as ~21.6 min / month for a 30-day month.

If you want this applied to actual NetworkDevice uptime/downtime in Probler I can pull the device uptime fields and compute the real downtime per month per device.
